title: Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain
summary: Beitris Bhàn walks up from Àth ìseal in the camp's first winter with her mother's knife and takes the end room of a house of spoil, next the well, to lay out the camp's dead. Within the week the first bodies are brought to her table.

title: The nine of the first winter
summary: Achadh dhomhain buries nine in its first winter: two hewers dead of the damp, a child crushed under a runaway cart of spoil, and six of the camp cough. Beitris Bhàn cuts the turf for each grave herself, the camp having no man yet spared from the pit for the work.

title: The Company's coach put on the Ros dhomhain road
summary: The Company's twice-weekly coach begins running between the quay at Ros dhomhain and the camps of Muileann chrom, carrying clerks and overseers dry-shod with their ledgers on their knees. The crews whose labour fills the ledgers walk the same road on foot, in whatever weather it gives them.

title: The steelyard changes the count
summary: After the Company's great steelyard is hung at Ros dhomhain, the custodians' old count of the yield, kept in baskets and seasons of a crew's labour, is entered less and less in the rolls, until it is not entered at all. Ùna nic Choinnich says the island has let the wrong hill be written down.

title: The wreck off Ros dhìreach
summary: Ros dhìreach's first cargo goes down in a squall within a mile of the new coal stage, taking the boat and two of the crew who had gone out to trim her load. The fishermen whose grounds were given over for the stage will not put out past the wreck for a season after.

title: The camp hears of the first steamer
summary: Word comes up the coal road to Achadh dhomhain of a Company ship at Ros dhomhain driven by no sail, with a wheel turning at either side and smoke instead of spray, which the harbour's fishermen row out in a ring to look at. It is said in the camp that within a few years the Company will send nothing else.

title: A boy of the deep gallery will not stop shaking
summary: In the camp's second winter a young hewer of Donnchadh mac Thormoid's crew comes up from the deep gallery shaking and says something stood in the draught without stirring. His crew-mates laugh him down as cold and dark playing him false; Donnchadh says nothing at all, which Beitris Bhàn afterward remembers longer than the boy's fright.

title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table
summary: At a laying-out in the camp's fourth winter, Donnchadh mac Thormoid's wife tells the sitting women, for the first time outside her own house, what her husband met in the deep gallery and what it charged him to keep, and what passed the night their daughter was born. She says the words are his and she will change none of them.

title: The women's rule of silence
summary: Beitris Bhàn tells the women who sat the night of the telling that a charge laid on a man by a spirit is not theirs to spend on the camp's talk, whatever they make of the child in their own kitchens. No meeting is called and no vote taken, but the rule holds among them for years.

title: The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness
summary: Season on season the women who handle the camp's dying by hand and wrist and throat notice, before anyone else in Achadh dhomhain, that Aisling is not changing as a growing child should: no tooth lost and regrown, no wrist outgrowing last year's sleeve, no voice dropping.

title: Ùna nic Choinnich dies at Muileann chiar
summary: Ùna nic Choinnich dies in her own bed at Muileann chiar, eighty-five years old, having led the silver guild since before the strangers' fever and twice put the Company's offers to a show of hands and twice seen them refused. Achadh dhomhain, which never saw her, mourns her by the sayings that came down the road ahead of the coach.

title: The first coal from every gallery at Cill dhìreach
summary: At Cill dhìreach the custodians keep the shrine where every crew brings the first piece cut from a new gallery before the rest goes to the steelyard, and the Company suffers the custom, for a stone of coal a gallery costs it little.

title: Beitris Bhàn's first climb to Cill ghlas
summary: Beitris Bhàn climbs the hill path to Cill ghlas for the first time at Lùnastal and sets a single piece of coal by the flame at the mouth of the oldest cutting, more from the habit of a hard winter's laying-out than from any settled custom of her own people. She says nothing to the custodian, and the custodian says nothing to her.
